**Parent:** LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI (When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer)
**Type:** docs · **Priority:** medium
**Depends on:** the E2E retry-timer verification test sibling (test-first ordering)

## Problem

`proxy/README.md` documents the exhaustion 503 contract, the client-facing
retry-timer cap (`server.max_retry_after_seconds`, default 3600 s) and the
chain-hold bound, but it does **not** state the retry contract as an
end-to-end-verified guarantee and does not state the client expectation (that
the ContextHub client honours the full advertised hint up to its own long
ceiling, rather than clamping to 60 s). Without this the verified contract is
not discoverable, and the relationship between the capped advertisement and
the client wait is ambiguous.

## Change

Update `proxy/README.md` (and the relevant `provider.py` comments) to state the
verified "no models available" retry contract and the client expectation,
pointing at the end-to-end verification test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, `proxy/README.md` (the exhaustion/retry
  contract section), and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- `proxy/README.md` states the verified contract explicitly (truthful `Retry-After` + matching `retry_after`, capped-advertisement vs unbounded-true-wait distinction, both `code` variants, bounded-hold guarantee) and names the end-to-end verification test as the regression guard.
- The README documents the client expectation (ContextHub honours the full advertised hint via `serverHintMaxDelayMs`, default 6 h, referencing WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM) without contradicting the advertisement-cap section, and records the docs/wiki scan outcome.

## Minimal implementation

- Edit the "All Providers Exhausted" section (~line 690) and the "Client-facing retry-timer cap" subsection to add a short "Verified retry contract" paragraph plus the client expectation.
- Add a one-line comment/docstring reference in `provider.py` naming `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`.
- Search `docs/` and the wiki for related exhaustion/retry pages; update or confirm no change needed and record the outcome.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the E2E retry-timer verification test item (document the verified contract only once it is pinned).

## Key Files

- `proxy/README.md` — exhaustion / retry contract sections (~line 690 and the "Client-facing retry-timer cap" subsection).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — comments on `_compute_retry_after` / `_build_exhausted_response` / `_build_time_window_exhausted_response`.

## Deliverables

- Updated README + code-comment diff.
- A short note recording the docs/wiki scan outcome.
data.title: Document verified no-models retry contract and client expectation

# Parse attribution markers in log_parser.py

## Goal

Teach `log_parser.py` to parse the actor/source attribution markers
added by **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** into structured fields on restart and
mode-switch LogEvents, degrading gracefully when markers are absent.

## Scope

- Add two new fields to `LogEvent`: `source` (str | None) and `actor`
  (str | None). The existing `reason` field is reused to carry the
  attribution `reason=` value on restart/mode-switch events (it is
  currently always `None` for these kinds, so reuse is backward compatible).
- Parse `source=scheduler|worker|api|manual` from:
  - `Mode-switch restart spawned:` lines (attribution appended at
    `set_mode()` time)
  - Mode-switch lines (`Mode scheduler: applied scheduled mode ...` and
    `Grandfathering: enabled; ...`)
  - The `start-proxy.sh --restart` startup attribution line (reason echoed
    into the new process startup log before the `Starting LLama Proxy Server`
    marker)
- Parse `actor=<name>` and `reason=<text>` from the same lines.
- When markers are absent, the fields remain `None` (existing behaviour
  preserved).
- Add tolerant regex extractors (`source=`, `actor=`, `reason=`) so any
  future key=value attribution fields are easy to add.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `log_parser.py` parses the new attribution markers into structured
      fields on the restart/mode-switch events (absent markers degrade
      gracefully to the current behaviour).
- [ ] `LogEvent.source` / `LogEvent.actor` are populated and `LogEvent.reason`
      carries the attribution reason when markers are present on restart and
      mode-switch lines.
- [ ] When markers are absent, the new fields default to `None` (backward
      compatible; existing tests unchanged).
- [ ] A tolerant regex pattern extracts `source=`, `actor=`, and `reason=`
      from arbitrary log lines.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: markers present on spawned/complete/startup lines,
      markers absent (historical log), missing individual keys.
- [ ] No regression in existing log-line parsing (all existing tests still pass).

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`

## Dependencies

- **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** — the attribution markers must be produced by
  the proxy first; verify the exact landed marker format before finalising
  the extractors.
data.title: Parse attribution markers in log_parser.py

data.description:
## Problem

Pi displays the proxy's `X-Resolved-Model` response header as the model string. That header is built as `<provider>/<model>` in two places:

- `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` `_resolved_model_header` (LP-0MR4ZIGDT004A3E1)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` `_build_resolved_model_value` / `_add_resolved_model_header`

Both prefer the config `provider` brand field and only fall back to the entry `name` when `provider` is absent. As a result, the free-tier entry `munitoai-free` (and its paid sibling `munitoai`, which share `provider: MunitoAI` and `model: deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`) both report `MunitoAI/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`. The "free" marker exists only in the entry `name`, the `api_key_env` (`MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY`), and the auth.json key stem (`munitoai_free`) — none of which enter the display path (introduced by LP-0MRC4G7ZL005L1BO, "use actual provider name, not provider entry name").

Operators therefore cannot tell free-tier from paid-tier service in Pi, and requests appear to "bypass" the free tier even when they are served by it.

## Goal

Make the `X-Resolved-Model` header (and any equivalent chunk/display path) distinguish provider **tiers** (free vs paid) without losing the provider-brand attribution added in LP-0MRC4G7ZL005L1BO. Design target: a tier-aware display — e.g. the free MunitoAI entry resolves to a string containing `free` (such as `MunitoAI Free/...`) while the paid entry keeps its paid label — without touching failure-domain, cooldown, or usage-limit quarantine keys (which key on entry name / API-key account and must stay unchanged).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A request served by `munitoai-free` returns an `X-Resolved-Model` header whose human-readable provider component conveys the `free` tier (e.g. `MunitoAI Free/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` or a tier-carrying equivalent), while `munitoai` (paid) returns the paid label.
- AC2: The two MunitoAI entries produce **distinct** `X-Resolved-Model` strings; free and paid are no longer byte-identical.
- AC3: `_build_resolved_model_value` (provider.py) and `_resolved_model_header` (proxy_remote.py) share the same tier-resolution logic via a single helper (a new config field such as `display_name`, or a rule that includes the entry `name` when it encodes a tier). No duplicated or divergent logic between the two sites.
- AC4: Failure-domain keys, entry cooldown keys, brand cooldown keys, usage-limit account keys, and `X-Provider` header values are **unchanged** — the change is display-only.
- AC5: Config option preferred over code special-casing "MunitoAI": the change must not hard-code provider names or `free` detection in Python; it must work for any entry via config.
- AC6: Tests: existing `proxy/tests/test_resolved_model_header.py` still passes; new/adjusted tests assert (a) free entry emits the tier-carrying display string, (b) paid entry emits its distinct string, (c) headers for local providers (`local/<model>`) are unchanged, (d) failure-domain/cooldown keys unaffected.

## References

- LP-0MR4ZIGDT004A3E1 — Show the model being used in Pi (origin of X-Resolved-Model)
- LP-0MRC4G7ZL005L1BO — Fix X-Resolved-Model header format: use actual provider name, not provider entry name (the behaviour this item refines)
- LP-0MV5UPXKL002MSKB / LP-0MV6ENYYH006XX0Z — MunitoAI provider additions / tier placement
data.title: Make X-Resolved-Model tier-aware so free MunitoAI is distinguishable from paid in Pi
